goal:
Build a tool that turns a CSV of daily sales into a printable PDF report.

Invoked as `python -m salesreport data.csv --out report.pdf`, it produces a multi-page PDF containing: a title page with the report name, the date range covered and the row count; a summary table of totals and averages per product; a bar chart of revenue per product and a line chart of revenue over time; and a final page listing any rows that were skipped because they could not be parsed, or a line stating that none were.

The document has to look designed rather than dumped: a consistent typographic hierarchy, page margins, a header or footer carrying the page number, table rules or banding that make rows scannable, axis labels and units on both charts, and a restrained colour palette used consistently across the charts and the table.

Failures are handled like a real tool: a missing input file, an unreadable file, a CSV with none of the expected columns, and an output path that cannot be written each produce one clear message on stderr and a non-zero exit status, never a traceback.

The CSV has columns `date,product,units,unit_price`. Revenue is units times unit_price. Include a pytest suite that covers the aggregation maths on a fixture, the skipped-row accounting, and the failure cases.

checks.why: the PDF library it needs was worked out and declared, not wished for
the run recorded what it resolved
it really writes a PDF a reader can open

printf 'date,product,units,unit_price
2024-01-01,widget,3,2.50
2024-01-02,widget,4,2.50
2024-01-02,gadget,1,10.00
2024-01-03,gadget,2,10.00
' > /tmp/sales_probe.csv && rm -f /tmp/sales_probe.pdf && python -m salesreport /tmp/sales_probe.csv --out /tmp/sales_probe.pdf >/dev/null 2>&1 && head -c 5 /tmp/sales_probe.pdf | grep -q '%PDF' && [ $(wc -c < /tmp/sales_probe.pdf) -gt 5000 ]
